title: Council declares Kitchener regional seat vacant
subtitle: Also: fuel contract, watermain cost increases, Speedsville Road transfer, advisory appointments, and anti-hate service funding request.
overview: Regional Council declared the Kitchener regional councillor seat, formerly held by Rob Deutschmann, vacant. Council also directed the Regional Clerk to bring a report on options for filling it to a special meeting on March 4, 2025. An amendment moved the date from February 11 so the report can reflect the provincial election results {{vote:m12}}. The declaration then passed {{vote:m13}}. Until the seat is filled, Kitchener has one fewer regional voice at the table.

Council also approved a five-year gasoline and diesel fuel contract with Suncor Energy Products Partnership worth $69,857,074.30, and cost increases on the Kitchener East Side Watermain contracts. It started the process to transfer Speedsville Road in Cambridge to the Region, approved an updated Public Art Policy, and wrote off $118,966.89 in uncollected accounts. Appointments were made to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee, the Administrative Penalties Program and the Library Committee.

Delegates from the Coalition of Muslim Women asked for ongoing funding for their anti-hate service; no motion followed. Councillor Colleen James announced a leave of absence to run in the provincial election.

decisions.detail: Council declared the Regional Councillor – Kitchener seat vacant and directed the Regional Clerk to report on options for filling it at a special meeting on March 4, 2025.
Council amended the motion to move the special meeting on filling the vacancy from February 11 to March 4, 2025.
Council accepted Suncor Energy Products Partnership's tender for a five-year contract from March 1, 2025, worth $69,857,074.30 plus taxes, with options to renew for three more one-year periods.
Council increased the construction contract with Regional Sewer and Watermain Ltd. to $3,811,667.67 and the consulting contract with CIMA Canada Inc. to $459,909.00, both plus taxes.
Council approved starting the process to transfer Speedsville Road between Maple Grove Road and Eagle Street from the City of Cambridge to the Region, including public notice and by-law amendments.

Council appointed seven members to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee, three Administrative Penalties Program hearing officers, and four community representatives to the Library Committee.

decisions.item: Public Art Policy and receivables write-off
decisions.detail: Council approved the updated Public Art Policy and wrote off $118,966.89 in accounts receivable for 2024.
Council authorized the Chief Financial Officer to borrow funds on a temporary basis in 2025 to meet operating and capital expenditure needs.

debate: On the vacancy report date, the amendment's supporters argued council should know the provincial election results first, since one or two vacancies could change which option is best. They noted the legal deadline allows time, and that the amendment passed {{vote:m12}}.

Staff said the original February 11 date would give more lead time, especially if council chose an application process or a by-election. A March 4 date would tighten that time, though staff said they could work with it. Under the Municipal Act, council has 60 days from the declaration to appoint or pass a by-election by-law.

One councillor suggested a February report with options for one or two vacancies. The Regional Chair opposed the amendment, saying the debate should happen in public sooner, though any decision would still follow the election.

Delegates from the Coalition of Muslim Women said the anti-hate service began with provincial seed funding and later Regional support. Its coordinator has gone from full time to part time. They estimated about $120,000 a year, or half that for six months, to bridge a gap until expected funding in the summer.

On speed cameras, a councillor raised a Lobsinger Line school zone where the limit steps down twice. Transportation staff said they would work with the township to revisit it as the program relaunches.
